statement: To legally change your name in New Mexico, you must be a New Mexico resident and file a Petition for Name Change in district court under Sections 40-8-1 through 40-8-3 NMSA 1978. If you are 14 or older you can file for yourself; if you are 13 or younger, your parent or legal guardian must file for you.
detail: The filing fee is $132.00. As part of the standard process, you also prepare an Order Sealing Final Order to Change Name for the judge to sign alongside your name-change order. New Mexico's court self-help instructions for an adult's own name change do not describe a newspaper-publication step; publication is described only as a way to notify an absent parent in a minor's name-change case.

cost.note: This is the district court filing fee. Certified copies cost $1.50 each, and recording your order with the county clerk costs $25.00.

topic: New Mexico driver's license or ID name change
statement: To update the name on your New Mexico driver's license or ID, bring your current license or ID, a certified copy of your court Order for Change of Name, and either your new Social Security card or an SSA printout showing your new name to the Motor Vehicle Division.
detail: If your license or ID doesn't already show your current address, bring proof of address too. The MVD mails your new card to the address on file. The fee is $18 for a four-year license or $34 for an eight-year license; people 75 and older aren't charged to renew.

cost.note: The fee depends on the license term: $18 for a four-year license or $34 for an eight-year license. Renewal is free for people 75 and older.

topic: New Mexico driver's license or ID gender designation
statement: To change the sex designation on a New Mexico driver's license or ID card, you complete a Request for Sex Designation Change (Form MVD-10237), have it notarized, and choose Male (M), Female (F), or (X), swearing under penalty of perjury that the request is to make your card accurately reflect your sex identity.
detail: The form asks for a court order, marriage certificate, or divorce decree only if you are also changing your name at the same time — it does not ask for any medical or court documentation to change the sex designation on its own. Submit the notarized form to a New Mexico Motor Vehicle Division Service Center.

source.title: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department, Motor Vehicle Division — Request for Sex Designation Change (Form MVD-10237)

topic: New Mexico birth certificate name change
statement: If you have a New Mexico court order changing your name, you can present it to the New Mexico Department of Vital Records and Health Statistics to request an amended birth certificate. You submit a birth certificate request form along with a certified copy of the court-ordered name change.
detail: New Mexico's courts cite $20.00 as the cost of an amended birth certificate among the overall costs of a name-change case.

cost.note: This is the fee New Mexico's courts cite for an amended birth certificate; confirm the current fee directly with Vital Records.

topic: New Mexico birth certificate gender designation
statement: Under a 2019 law (Senate Bill 20, effective October 29, 2019), a person born in New Mexico can request a new birth certificate showing Male, Female, or X as their gender designation by completing a notarized Request to Change Gender Designation on a Birth Certificate form — no physician's letter or surgery is required.
detail: If your current legal name is different from the name on your birth certificate, you must also submit a certified copy of your name-change court order. The fee is $20.00, which includes your new birth certificate; extra copies are $10.00 each. New Mexico's health department cautions that it is unsure whether other agencies, such as the passport office, will accept these amended certificates, and that nothing on the new record shows a change was made — so a court order might still be needed to use your new name and gender designation elsewhere.

cost.note: Includes one new birth certificate; additional copies are $10.00 each.

source.title: New Mexico Department of Health — Gender Designation Change (Vital Records)
